name: Dead Man's Hand
flavor: Aces and eights, face up on the table. Everyone at the game knows what that hand means, and so, now, do you.
description: You lay down a hand that should not exist — aces and eights, face up, in a fight nobody was playing cards in — and let its meaning land like a verdict. Choose one creature you can see within range. It makes a Constitution saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it takes [[6d8]] psychic damage as the certainty of its own death arrives ahead of schedule, and it is stunned until the end of your next turn. On a success it takes half as much damage and is not stunned. Either way it is hurt: this is the biggest thing you do all fight, and it does not hinge on one roll.
narration: You deal it out onto whatever surface is nearest — a table, a crate, the floor between you — and you do not have to explain it. Everyone at a table knows that hand. So, somehow, does the thing you dealt it to.
sheetSummary: Once per combat. Action, 30 ft, one creature, costs 4 Mayhem. Constitution save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[6d8]] psychic and stunned until the end of your next turn. Success: half damage, no stun.
